entry: Intense negative emotional response toward certain people, things or ideas. Hatred is closely associated with [[Anger|anger]], contempt and [[Disgust|disgust]], and is regarded as the opposite of [[Love|love]]. As an emotion it can be short-lived or long-lasting, and of low intensity ("I hate broccoli") or high ("I hate the whole world"). Robert Sternberg identified three elements: a negation of intimacy, an infusion of passion such as fear or anger, and a decision to devalue a previously valued object. [[Sigmund Freud]] defined hate as an ego state that wishes to destroy the source of its unhappiness. A hate crime is a criminal act that targets victims for their perceived membership in a social group, usually defined by race, gender, religion, sexual orientation or disability. Hate speech is perceived to disparage people on similar grounds.

Sixth [[Pharaoh|pharaoh]] of Egypt's Eighteenth Dynasty (r. c. 1479–1458 BC). Hatshepsut was the daughter of Thutmose I and the wife of her half-brother Thutmose II. After his death she served as regent for her stepson [[Thutmose III]], and within several years she took the full titulary of pharaoh as his co-ruler. She was Egypt's second confirmed woman to rule in her own right, after Sobekneferu. To establish her authority she was depicted with masculine traits and male garb, while emphasizing both male and female qualities. Her reign of about 21–22 years was prosperous and largely peaceful. She oversaw large-scale construction, including the Karnak Temple Complex and the Mortuary Temple of Hatshepsut at Deir el-Bahari. Later, her statues were destroyed, her monuments defaced, and many of her achievements credited to other pharaohs.

Vocaloid voicebank and software application developed by Crypton Future Media. Her voice is generated from vocal samples provided by Japanese voice actress Saki Fujita. Marketed as a virtual idol, her official mascot is a 16-year-old girl with turquoise twintails, and she performs at live concerts as an animated projection. Released on August 31, 2007, she was the first Japanese voicebank for Yamaha's Vocaloid platform. Her name means "the first sound of the future", and her code name CV01 marks her as the first of Crypton's Character Vocal Series.

Confederacy of Iroquoian [[Indigenous peoples|Indigenous peoples]] in northeast [[North America|North America]], also known as the Iroquois. The original Mohawk, Oneida, Onondaga, Cayuga and Seneca peoples were joined after 1722 by the Tuscarora, which is why the confederacy was also called the Six Nations. Its founding Great Law of Peace is traditionally attributed to the Great Peacemaker, Hiawatha, and Jigonhsasee. At its peak around 1700 its power extended from [[New York (state)|New York State]] into Ontario and Quebec, and south into Virginia and Kentucky. For nearly 200 years it held the balance of power between French and British colonies, and it backed the British in the [[French and Indian War|French and Indian War]]. During the [[American Revolution|American Revolution]] the confederacy split, with the Oneida and Tuscarora fighting for the Patriots. Many Haudenosaunee then fled to British Canada. Today they issue their own [[Passport|passports]] and consider themselves sovereign.

[[Dwarf planet|Dwarf planet]] beyond the orbit of [[Neptune|Neptune]], with two moons and a ring system. Two teams claim discovery credit, and it was named in 2008 after the Hawaiian goddess of childbirth and fertility. It is the third-largest known trans-Neptunian object, after [[Eris (dwarf planet)|Eris]] and [[Pluto|Pluto]], and its mass is about one-third that of Pluto. Its elongated shape and rapid rotation are thought to result from a giant collision that left it the largest member of a collisional family. In 2017 astronomers announced a ring system, the first found around a trans-Neptunian object. Its high [[Albedo|albedo]] comes from a surface of crystalline water ice.

Collection of states ruled by the Hausa people, between the [[Niger River|Niger River]] and [[Lake Chad|Lake Chad]] in present-day northern [[Nigeria|Nigeria]]. According to the Bayajidda legend, the Hausa states were founded by the sons of a [[Baghdad|Baghdadi]] prince who married Daurama, the last ruler of Daura. The seven "true" states, the Hausa Bakwai, were Biram, Daura, Gobir, Kano, Katsina, Rano and Zazzau, while seven others, the Hausa Banza, lay to their west and south. The kingdoms were built around fortified capitals and exported kola nuts, leather goods and textiles. Internal rivalries and warfare weakened them. In the Fulani jihad of 1804–1808, Usman dan Fodio conquered them and founded the [[Sokoto Caliphate|Sokoto Caliphate]].

Chadic language of the Afroasiatic family spoken across [[West Africa|West Africa]], and the most widely spoken language of the Chadic branch. Spoken by over 94.5 million people, it is tonal, using relative pitch to distinguish words and mark grammatical categories. Ethnologue estimated 58 million first-language and 36 million second-language speakers. Hausa is the sole official language of Niger, where it replaced French in 2025, and it is a [[Lingua franca|lingua franca]] across much of northern Nigeria, southern Niger, northern Cameroon, Ghana, Benin and Togo. It is written in a Romanized orthography and in [[Arabic script|Ajami]], an adaptation of the Arabic script. In Nigeria its film industry is known as Kannywood.

Capital and largest city of [[Cuba|Cuba]]. The most populous city in the Caribbean region and the largest by area, it had 2,142,939 inhabitants in 2021, and the capital city covers 728.26 km² (281.18 sq mi). Founded in 1519 by the [[Spanish Empire|Spanish Empire]], it overtook Santiago in the mid-16th century because of its harbor and became the island's capital in 1552. Walls and forts protected the harbor against naval attacks, and it became a stopping point for galleons returning to the [[Iberian Peninsula|Iberian Peninsula]]. Old Havana was declared a UNESCO [[World Heritage Site|World Heritage Site]] in 1982. The city is the seat of the Cuban government and home to more than 100 diplomatic offices. Its official population dropped to 1,749,964 by the end of 2024.

Island state of the [[United States|United States]] in the [[Pacific Ocean|Pacific Ocean]], about 2,000 miles (3,200 km) southwest of the mainland. Hawaii consists of 137 volcanic islands and is the only U.S. state in [[Oceania|Oceania]] and the only one that is an archipelago. Two-thirds of its residents live on Oʻahu, home to the capital, [[Honolulu|Honolulu]]. Settled by Polynesians between 1000 and 1200 CE, it was unified as a kingdom in 1810 and was overthrown by American and European businessmen in 1893. It was annexed by the U.S. in 1898 and became a state on August 21, 1959. [[James Cook|James Cook]] was the first known non-Polynesian to arrive, in 1778. Tourism and military defense are now its largest sectors. Its residents have the longest life expectancy of any U.S. state, at 80.7 years.

[[Archipelago|Archipelago]] of eight major volcanic islands, several atolls and numerous islets in the North [[Pacific Ocean|Pacific Ocean]]. Extending about 1,500 miles (2,400 km) from Hawaiʻi Island to Kure Atoll, the chain formed as the Pacific Plate moved northwestward over a [[Hotspot (geology)|hotspot]] in the mantle. The southeast island is volcanically active, while the older northwestern islands are smaller because of erosion. The U.S. state of Hawaii occupies almost the entire archipelago, the exception being [[Midway Atoll|Midway Atoll]]. The uninhabited Northwestern Hawaiian Islands form a national monument and World Heritage Site.

Hypothetical [[Black-body radiation|black-body radiation]] emitted by [[Black hole|black holes]] through quantum effects outside the [[Event horizon|event horizon]]. Predicted by [[Stephen Hawking|Stephen Hawking]] in 1974, it was not foreseen by earlier models that assumed nothing inside the event horizon could escape. It would reduce a black hole's mass and rotational energy, causing evaporation, which for all but the smallest black holes is extremely slow. Its temperature is inversely proportional to mass, so small primordial black holes would emit faster and could end in a burst of high-energy radiation. The radiation is far too faint for current [[Telescope|telescopes]] to detect, and such bursts have not been observed.

Dried grass, legumes or other herbaceous plants used as animal fodder. Cut and dried for storage, hay is fed to livestock such as [[Cattle|cattle]], [[Horse|horses]], [[Goat|goats]] and [[Sheep|sheep]], as well as to rabbits and guinea pigs. It is used when there is not enough pasture, when weather prevents grazing, such as in winter, or when an animal is kept in a [[Stable|stable]] or barn. Common plants include ryegrass, timothy, fescue, and legumes such as alfalfa and clover. Haymaking involves cutting, curing, raking, processing and storing, and it is highly sensitive to weather. Drought stunts seed and leaf production, and wet weather can spoil cut hay in the field or cause rot and toxins after baling.

Japanese animator, filmmaker and [[Manga|manga]] artist. He joined Toei Animation in 1963 and directed his first feature, *The Castle of Cagliostro*, in 1979. In 1985 he co-founded [[Studio Ghibli|Studio Ghibli]], for which he wrote and directed films including *Laputa: Castle in the Sky*, *My Neighbor Totoro*, *Kiki's Delivery Service* and *Princess Mononoke* (1997), the first animated film to win the Japan Academy Film Prize for Picture of the Year. *Spirited Away* (2001) became Japan's highest-grossing film and won the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature, as did *The Boy and the Heron* (2023). His works often explore humanity's relationship with nature and technology, and his protagonists are frequently strong girls or young women.

Ottoman corsair and later admiral of the [[Ottoman Empire|Ottoman]] navy. Born on [[Lesbos|Lesbos]], he began as a corsair under his elder brother Oruç Reis, and the brothers captured [[Algiers|Algiers]] from Spain in 1516. After Oruç's death in 1518 he inherited the nickname "Barbarossa" ("Redbeard"). In 1533 [[Suleiman the Magnificent|Suleiman the Magnificent]] appointed him Kapudan Pasha, or grand admiral. He conquered [[Tunis|Tunis]] in 1534, and at Preveza in 1538 his 122 galleys defeated a Holy League armada of 157 ships. He conducted joint campaigns with the French in the 1540s, and retired to Constantinople in 1545. His victories secured Ottoman dominance over the Mediterranean in the mid-16th century.

Self-censorship guidelines applied to most major U.S. studio films from 1934 to 1968. Formally the Motion Picture Production Code, it is named after Will H. Hays, president of the Motion Picture Producers and Distributors of America from 1922 to 1945. The studios adopted the code in 1930 and began rigidly enforcing it in 1934, when it was closely associated with Joseph Breen. It listed unacceptable content such as drugs, [[Profanity|profanity]] and sex. The code weakened under competition from [[Television|television]], foreign films, controversial directors and court rulings, and in 1968 it was replaced by the MPAA film rating system.

Edible nut of the hazel tree, especially the species *Corylus avellana*, also known as a cobnut or filbert. Hazelnuts are eaten as a snack and used in baking and desserts, and in confectionery such as praline and [[Chocolate|chocolate]] truffles, or in hazelnut spreads such as Nutella. Hazelnut oil, pressed from the nuts, is strongly flavored and high in monounsaturated fat, and is used for cooking and dressings. In 2023 [[Turkey|Turkey]] was the world's largest producer, accounting for 57.7% of total production. Evidence of large-scale [[Mesolithic|Mesolithic]] nut processing, some 8,000 years old, was found in a pit on the Scottish island of Colonsay. Nuts make up between 33.2% and 49.5% of the fruit, depending on the cultivar.

Cephalic part of an animal, usually containing the [[Brain|brain]] and the main sense organs. A head usually includes the ears, brain, eyes, nose and mouth, which aid hearing, sight, smell and taste. Some very simple animals have no head, but many bilaterally symmetric forms do. Heads develop through cephalization, in which nervous tissue and sense organs concentrate at the front of the body; in [[Bilateria|Bilateria]] this trend dates to some 555 million years ago. In humans the head consists of the skull, hyoid bone and cervical vertebrae. Insect heads bear eyes, antennae and mouthparts that vary greatly between species, making them useful for identification. Vertebrate heads have a bony skull clearly separated from the main body.

Highest official in the executive branch of a state. The head of government usually handles the day-to-day affairs of the state and leads its ministers. In many democratic systems the [[Head of state|head of state]] also holds this role, as with the [[President of the United States|president]] of the United States. In most parliamentary systems, including constitutional monarchies, the head of government is the de facto political leader and answers to at least one chamber of the legislature. In the [[United Kingdom|United Kingdom]] the prime minister runs the government while the monarch has a largely ceremonial role. In communist states the general secretary of the party is usually the supreme leader. In the Soviet Union, [[Joseph Stalin|Joseph Stalin]] held the premiership from 1941 to 1953, and [[Nikita Khrushchev|Nikita Khrushchev]] from 1958 to 1964. Under military dictatorships the military leader usually fills the role of head of state, head of government, or both.

Highest-ranking official of a [[Sovereign state|sovereign state]]. A head of state may be a monarch or a president, and may also be the [[Head of government|head of government]] or merely perform ceremonial duties. In parliamentary systems such as India or the United Kingdom the head of state usually has mostly ceremonial powers, while in presidential systems the head of state is also the head of government. Former French president [[Charles de Gaulle|Charles de Gaulle]] said the head of state should embody "the spirit of the nation". Semi-presidential systems, which first appeared in Finland and Germany in 1919, combine features of presidential and parliamentary models. Japan's constitution defines the emperor as "the symbol of the State and of the unity of the people", with no powers related to government.

Mythical archetype of a rider on horseback who is missing his head. Such figures have appeared in [[Folklore|folklore]] across [[Europe|Europe]] since the [[Middle Ages|Middle Ages]]. In Irish folklore the dullahan is a demonic fairy who carries his head under his arm, and a name he calls signals that person's death. Washington Irving's 1820 short story *The Legend of Sleepy Hollow* made the figure a famous American character. It was later adapted in the 1999 film *Sleepy Hollow*, directed by [[Tim Burton|Tim Burton]].

Australian external territory of sub-Antarctic volcanic islands in the southern [[Indian Ocean|Indian Ocean]]. Discovered in the 1850s, the uninhabited territory lies on the Kerguelen Plateau and contains Australia's only active volcanoes. Heard Island is dominated by Big Ben, a stratovolcano topped by Mawson Peak, and about 70 percent of the island is covered by glaciers. The islands support more than one million breeding pairs of macaroni penguins, about 20 percent of the world's total, as well as elephant seals and Antarctic fur seals. Managed as a nature reserve, the territory has been a [[World Heritage Site|World Heritage Site]] since 1997.

Sensory perception of sound by living organisms through the detection of pressure vibrations in a surrounding medium. Sound may be heard through solid, liquid or gaseous matter, and hearing is one of the traditional five senses. In humans and other vertebrates it is performed by the [[Auditory system|auditory system]]. The outer ear funnels sound to the eardrum, the ossicles of the middle ear transmit the vibrations to the cochlea, and hair cells in the organ of Corti convert them into nerve impulses. The basilar membrane is tonotopic, so each frequency resonates at a characteristic place, with high frequencies at the base of the cochlea. The impulses are perceived by the [[Brain|brain]], primarily in the temporal lobe. Partial or total inability to hear is called [[Hearing loss|hearing loss]].

Partial inability to hear, or total inability termed deafness. Hearing loss may be present at birth or acquired later, and may affect one or both ears. Causes include [[Genetics|genetics]], aging, noise exposure, some infections, birth complications, trauma, and certain medications or toxins. Infections during pregnancy, such as [[Rubella|rubella]] and [[Syphilis|syphilis]], may cause it in a child. Hearing loss is diagnosed when a person cannot hear 25 [[Decibel|decibels]] in at least one ear, and severity ranges from mild (25 to 40 dB) to profound (greater than 90 dB). About half of hearing loss globally is preventable through immunization, avoiding loud noise and avoiding certain medications. Hearing aids, [[Sign language|sign language]] and cochlear implants can help.

Syndrome caused by an impairment in the [[Heart|heart]]'s ability to fill with and pump blood. Also called congestive heart failure, it typically causes shortness of breath, excessive fatigue and swelling of the legs. Common causes include [[Coronary artery disease|coronary artery disease]], heart attack, high blood pressure and [[Atrial fibrillation|atrial fibrillation]]. Treatment usually includes lifestyle changes such as not smoking, exercise and diet, plus medicines. Severe cases may require a pacemaker, a ventricular assist device or transplantation. About 40 million people had heart failure worldwide in 2015, affecting about 2% of adults and more than 10% of those over 70.

1899 novella by Polish-British novelist [[Joseph Conrad|Joseph Conrad]]. Sailor Charles Marlow recounts his assignment as steamer captain for a Belgian company in the African interior, where he is sent to find Kurtz, an ivory trader who has "gone native". The novella does not name its river, but at the time the [[Congo Free State|Congo Free State]], a private colony of Belgium's King Leopold II, was the setting. It is widely regarded as a critique of [[Colonialism|colonialism]] and implicitly comments on imperialism and [[Racism|racism]]. Nigerian author [[Chinua Achebe|Chinua Achebe]] argued in 1975 that its depiction of Africans reinforced racist stereotypes. Defenders counter that its horror targets imperial barbarism universally. It inspired Francis Ford Coppola's 1979 film *Apocalypse Now*.
